reviewType: independent read-only source and actual screenshot review
status: MRI and separate native MRA visual reviews complete
observedImprovements: Segmentation presentation replaces the opaque pale head with a translucent gray source context; the cyan tumor becomes distinguishable in the same superior-oblique camera.
The lateral camera exposes the tumor shape more clearly and fills more of the main pane, making the comparison to the reference profile more useful.
Thin cyan tumor contours on linked grayscale slices retain more source texture than the previous filled overlays.
Compact presentation buttons and collapsed display settings leave the primary structure controls visible and preserve the surgical navigation entry.
sourceFaithfulness: T1CE remains explicitly identified; the screen says estimated structures and no acquired angiography. The estimated-alignment banner remains visible.
All four primary source structure checkboxes remain checked, including vessels and bone. Disconnected source estimates remain visible rather than silently deleted for resemblance.
Reviewed presentation code changes display settings, colors, and opacity without changing acquired arrays, segmentation masks, source identities, or registration acceptance.
MRI/MRA cannot activate CT transfer thresholds. The reference CTA appearance is not evidence of CT acquisition, vascular completeness, or accepted fusion in this study.
remainingVisibleLimits: This is closer in layout, translucency, and tumor contrast, but does not visually match the reference: the complete checked vessel estimate remains a dense rust network and contains conspicuous inferior/peripheral fragments.

The reference uses a vivid magenta brain boundary and a cleaner dark tissue interior. The application currently shows a neutral translucent brain/head with residual gray haze and a mottled cyan tumor surface.
MPR source heads occupy approximately 55–65 percent of each tile height, visibly less than in the reference. Expanding a slice is available; untested image stretching or cropping is not warranted.
The reference patient, acquisition field of view, selected structures, and lesion differ, so shape resemblance cannot be used as an anatomy correctness test.
resolvedCodeReviewFindings: New presentation/sliceOverlay settings initially failed persistence validation; both validators now accept supported enums and reject malformed choices. Root is adding native save/package/open and legacy round-trip regressions.
The volume heading is now gated by volumeDisplayed for modeled, passive, and rehearsal modes. The final rebuilt screenshot of those modes is outside this MRI screenshot review.
accuracyLimit: Appearance, interaction evidence, and source-preservation review only. Anatomical and clinical accuracy, vessel completeness, and clinical suitability are not established.

mraReview.source: IXI265-Guys-0845 acquired MRA, separate native collection
observedImprovements: Rust vessel-reference branches remain distinct against a faint neutral acquired MR context in both oblique and lateral views; source texture remains visible beneath the structure layer.
The interface retains the reference-like hierarchy of a large interactive 3D view with stacked linked MPR tiles, black background, and compact source/presentation controls.
The screen explicitly labels MRA, bright signal with no CT bone, Full source scope, and Published Derived Vessel Reference · Incomplete.
faithfulness: The abrupt inferior/superior limits in lateral and orthogonal views are consistent with the acquired 100-slice, approximately 80 mm MRA slab. They are a source-coverage limitation, not evidence of complete head/neck anatomy.

The rust geometry is a published derived, incomplete vessel reference with 199 disconnected components. Neutral bright voxels in the MRA are acquired signal; the display does not establish artery/vein classification or vascular completeness.
No CT skull, CT bone, tumor, or accepted T1 fusion is present in this MRA collection. The same-person T1 is a separate source and has not been added as accepted fusion.

The inspected report passes all 12 checks with no renderer errors. The original manifest plus two source arrays have identical before/after hash inventories, and the current manifest matches the source-QC receipt.
remainingVisibleLimits: This is an MR vascular slab, not the full CT head/neck and bone presentation shown in the CTA reference. That source difference correctly remains visible.
The lateral slab occupies a relatively small central region of the 3D pane, with large empty margins; this is usable through zoom but is less immediately immersive than the CTA reference.
Incomplete branch geometry and hard acquisition boundaries remain visible; they should not be extended, filled, smoothed into continuity, or silently removed to improve resemblance.

performance.judgment: Measured MRA navigation is usable for interactive inspection at approximately 31 median delivered FPS, with occasional slower frames and refinement completing within about 0.40 s in this run. This is not evidence of sustained 60 FPS, equivalent performance on other machines, or measured parity with Medivis. The combined reported current process memory is approximately 1.33 GiB; memory remains material for larger or denser studies.
